chapter: Philadelphia, Detroit and back to Atlantic City
title: Back East with a Dixieland band and the West Indian clarinetist Edwards
summary: Returning in spring 1921 he adds clarinet, saxophone and trumpet, drops Jimmy Harrison who read poorly, and gets endings and introductions for tunes.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: And we didn't have any arrangement on them, but I used to try to make endings, you know? A new ending or give it a little introduction to try to make it sound like something. And when we got back East, I still improved on that. Because, now when we got back East, I had a clarinet. And a saxophone. Saxophone and I played clarinet. And I had the trumpet and I had a regular Dixieland band then, see.
Who was the clarinet and saxophone player?
Well, I had a fellow -- no, I had a fellow [WALTER] a West Indian fellow named Edwards. He was good.
In a way, but he didn't have the swing that men like Buster Bailey -- he knew his instrument, but he didn't have the swing.
See, Jimmy Harrison didn't come back with us. And I wasn't particular about Jimmy Harrison, either, because now I was thinking seriously about having a band and Jimmy didn't read well.
I see. But when you then went back to Atlantic City, was it still 1920, or was it now 1921?
Well, I think it was the beginning of 1921. It was in the Spring.
